Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

opportunity noun

also chance (an opportunity), a chance to, take the opportunity, seize the chance, miss the chance, give someone a chance, occasion (an opportunity), should the occasion arise, if occasion should arise, if the opportunity arises, if I get the chance, when the chance offers, if the chance arises, make hay while the sun shines, carpe diem, seize the day

classical

Publil. Sent. O 31: occāsiō aegrē offertur, facile āmittitur
Liv. 22.39.21: neque occāsiōnī tuae dēsīs
Traupman 92, 269: occāsiōnem nancīscī, take the opportunity

occāsiō, occāsiōnis f.

noun, third declension

an opportunity, the right moment

To seize it: occāsiōnem rapere (Hor.) or nancīscī; to miss it, occāsiōnī deesse (Livy); to lose it, āmittere; when the chance comes, occāsiōne datā (Phaedr.).

Other words

  • potestās, potestātis f. — the chance (to do something), leave

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 10.13.1: ut prīmum potestās data est augendae dignitātis tuae; Traupman 95, 289: mihi nōn potestātem dedit respondendī, he didn’t give me a chance to answer

    Usually with a gerund in the genitive. To give someone the chance: potestātem facere (Cic. Cat. 3.11, Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Occāsiō aegrē offertur, facile āmittitur.

    An opportunity is hard to come by and easy to lose.Publil. Sent. O 31

  • rapiāmus, amīcī, occāsiōnem dē diē

    friends, let’s seize the chance the day gives usHor. Epod. 13.3–4

  • neque occāsiōnī tuae dēsīs neque suam occāsiōnem hostī dēs

    don’t miss your opportunity, and don’t give the enemy hisLiv. 22.39.21

  • vōs modo, inquit, parcite; occāsiōne rūrsus ērumpam datā

    “just keep quiet for me,” he said; “when I get the chance I’ll slip out again”Phaedr. 2.8.8–9

  • Sī fuerit occāsiō …

    If the occasion should arise …Traupman 105

  • rem inmātūram nisi per occāsiōnem aperīre nōluerat

    he had not wanted to reveal the plan before it was ripe, except when the chance offeredLiv. 1.5.5 (Lewis & Short s.v. occāsiō)

  • Occāsiōnem amplectere!

    Make hay while the sun shines!Traupman 326

  • dum loquimur, fūgerit invida aetās: carpe diem, quam minimum crēdula posterō

    while we talk, envious time will have fled: seize the day, trusting as little as you can to tomorrowHor. C. 1.11.7–8

See also chance, happen, possibility.
